name: Unknown Arbitrum LP manager public withdraw swaps user positions with no minimum output
summary: Two byte-identical unverified Uniswap V3 WETH/USDC position managers, 0x09c12514 and 0x3b329559, let any caller run withdraw(user, liquidity), which removes the user's position and sells its WETH via SwapRouter with amountOutMinimum 0. The attacker flash-borrowed WETH, crashed the pool price, forced withdraw for all 11 open positions, then swapped back.
notes: Direct, non-upgradeable runtimes; the anchor ran withdraw on both siblings, so both are targets and the later deployment (0x09c12514) sets the age. Operator collectFees and re-range calls change positions, not authorization or slippage; an earlier third-party withdraw (0x732260ca) paid its user in full.

The 11 positions were worth 78.611616 WETH and 23,815.920221 USDC (principal plus uncollected fees) at the pre-exploit pool state; users got 783.590805 USDC back, which the USDC component nets. An independent principal-only recomputation gives 78.34 WETH and 23,093 USDC.

The managers have no verified source. Selector names come from the public signature database. The missing caller check and zero minimum are established from the exploit trace (calldata of withdraw and exactInputSingle), not from source text.
